chunks.title: Bubble Sort
chunks.text:
// Bubble Sort

fun Bubble_Sort(@init<table> a):
    n = length(a)
    for (i = 0; i < n - 1; i += 1):
        changed = 0
        for (j = 0; j < n - i - 1; j += 1):
            if (a[j] > a[j + 1]):
                swap(a[j], a[j + 1])
                changed = 1
            end if
        end for
        if (changed == 0):
            break
        end if
    end for
    return a
end fun

chunks.title: Insertion Sort
chunks.text:
// Insertion Sort

fun Insertion_Sort(@init<table> a):
    for (i = 1; i < length(a); i += 1):
        key = a[i]
        j = i - 1
        while (j >= 0 and a[j] > key):
            a[j + 1] = a[j]
            j -= 1
        end while
        a[j + 1] = key
    end for
    return a
end fun

chunks.title: Selection Sort
chunks.text:
// Selection Sort

fun Selection_Sort(@init<table> a):
    n = length(a)
    for (i = 0; i < n - 1; i += 1):
        minimum = i
        for (j = i + 1; j < n; j += 1):
            if (a[j] < a[minimum]):
                minimum = j
            end if
        end for
        swap(a[i], a[minimum])
    end for
    return a
end fun

chunks.title: Lomuto Partition
chunks.text:
// Lomuto Partition

fun Lomuto_Partition(@init<table> a, low, high):
    pivot = a[high]
    i = low - 1
    for (j = low; j < high; j += 1):
        if (a[j] < pivot):
            i += 1
            swap(a[i], a[j])
        end if
    end for
    swap(a[i + 1], a[high])
    return i + 1
end fun

chunks.title: Hoare Partition
chunks.text:
// Hoare Partition

fun Hoare_Partition(@init<table> a, low, high):
    pivot = a[low]
    i = low - 1
    j = high + 1
    while (true):
        i += 1
        while (a[i] < pivot):
            i += 1
        end while
        j -= 1
        while (a[j] > pivot):
            j -= 1
        end while
        if (i >= j):
            return j
        end if
        swap(a[i], a[j])
    end while
end fun

chunks.title: Search and insertion reasoning
chunks.license: Project-authored explanations; team license review pending
chunks.text: Binary search needs an ascending sorted array because each midpoint comparison must justify discarding one side. If the target is smaller than the midpoint value, every value to its right is at least that midpoint value, so the target cannot be there. The opposite comparison discards the left side. On unsorted input, those exclusions are invalid and the search can miss a value that is present.

chunks.title: Search and insertion reasoning
chunks.license: Project-authored explanations; team license review pending
chunks.text: Insertion sort saves a[i] in a temporary key before shifting larger elements of the sorted prefix one position to the right. A shift can overwrite the original a[i] location. The saved key preserves the value being inserted until it can be placed at j + 1. Without that saved value, the algorithm can duplicate a shifted element and lose the original insertion value.
chunks.locator: Insertion sort: preserve the value being inserted

chunks.title: AVP language syntax
chunks.license: Project-authored explanations; grammar attribution in ATTRIBUTION.md
chunks.text:
AVP for-loop syntax uses an initialization, a condition and an update inside parentheses, followed by a colon. Put the body on new lines and close the block with end for. Use i < length(a) to visit indexes 0 through length(a) - 1. Semicolons separate the header fields; commas are also accepted by this grammar.

```avp
a = arr[4, 9, 7]
total = 0
for (i = 0; i < length(a); i += 1):
    total += a[i]
end for
result = total
```

chunks.title: AVP language syntax
chunks.license: Project-authored explanations; grammar attribution in ATTRIBUTION.md
chunks.text:
Define an AVP function with fun Name(parameters):, then a newline and the function body. Close it with end fun. A return expression sends a value back to the caller and exits that call. Call the function by its name with arguments in parentheses.

```avp
fun Twice(x):
    return x * 2
end fun
result = Twice(5)
```

chunks.title: AVP language syntax
chunks.license: Project-authored explanations; grammar attribution in ATTRIBUTION.md
chunks.text:
Create an AVP array with arr followed by comma-separated values in square brackets. Use a[index] to read or update one element. Array indexes start at 0, so a[0] is the first element and length(a) - 1 is the last valid index. This example changes the second element without replacing the whole array.

```avp
a = arr[4, 9, 7]
first = a[0]
a[1] = 8
result = first
```

chunks.title: AVP language syntax
chunks.license: Project-authored explanations; grammar attribution in ATTRIBUTION.md
chunks.text:
In AVP, = assigns a value while == compares values for equality. An if condition ends with a colon; its body starts on the next line and closes with end if. An optional else introduces the other branch. The comparison operators include ==, !=, <, <=, > and >=.

```avp
x = 5
if (x == 5):
    result = 1
else:
    result = 0
end if
```
